Simulated example data

Source: R/example-data.R
cr_example_data.Rd

A small simulated data set so the examples in the documentation and vignettes run without any files. It has repeated measures (k observations for each of n_id participants), a three-level between-person condition, a continuous and a binary outcome, and a random participant intercept, which makes it suitable for mixed models. The effects are arbitrary; do not read anything into them.

Usage

cr_example_data(n_id = 80, k = 4, seed = 42)

Arguments

n_id

Number of participants.

k

Observations per participant.

seed

Random seed. The global random-number state is left unchanged.

Value

A data frame with n_id * k rows and columns id (factor), condition (factor: Control, Gain, Loss), age, female (logical), trust and score (continuous outcomes), and share and bought (binary outcomes).

Examples

d <- cr_example_data()
head(d)
#>   id condition age female    trust share    score bought
#> 1  1   Control  41   TRUE 5.572484     1 1.623653      1
#> 2  1   Control  41   TRUE 3.240904     1 2.741360      0
#> 3  1   Control  41   TRUE 3.536337     0 1.900393      1
#> 4  1   Control  41   TRUE 4.321342     1 1.345710      1
#> 5  2   Control  43   TRUE 2.261628     1 2.971164      1
#> 6  2   Control  43   TRUE 2.895940     1 2.013496      1
res <- clean_regress(d, dvs = c(trust = "linear"), predictors = ~ condition)
res
#> ──────────────────────────────────────────────── 
#>                              Trust             
#>                              Linear            
#>                     b        95% CI        p   
#> ──────────────────────────────────────────────── 
#> Intercept          3.40    [3.17, 3.62]   < .001
#> Condition                                       
#>   Control (ref.)     —                          
#>   Gain             0.41    [0.08, 0.74]    .015 
#>   Loss             -0.24   [-0.65, 0.16]   .241 
#> Model fit                                       
#>   Observations      320                         
#>   R²               0.04                         
#>   AIC             1101.51                       
#> ──────────────────────────────────────────────── 
#> Note. b = unstandardized coefficient; CI = confidence
#> interval. CIs and p-values use HC3 robust SEs. (ref.) marks
#> the reference category for each factor.
